title: Telemetry weave: operator-lens notebook
content:
Purpose and framing:
This is a working notebook for the idea we started calling the "telemetry weave": a small set of consistent signals and view patterns that let an oncall/operator pivot quickly from a dashboard alert to a minimal set of traces and probe contexts needed to troubleshoot inference-layer incidents. Aim: reduce mean time to diagnose (MTTD) for token-latency and KV-cache related degradation without exploding trace volumes or dashboard clutter.

Quick definition (working):
- Telemetry weave = curated mapping between dashboard widgets (operator-facing), canonical metrics, trace anchors, and a small set of synthetic probes/queries that reproduce the failure mode. Think of it as a five-point lens: widget -> metric -> span-anchor -> probe -> remediation checklist.

Why this is different from other obs docs:
- Focused on operator flows (what to click first, not only what to collect).
- Lightweight mapping (avoid comprehensive metric catalog).
- Emphasizes privacy-safe trace anchors (no raw prompt text) and small reproducible probes for local replay.

High-level operator flow (proto):
1) Dashboard alert fires (e.g., 95th token latency spike on model-route X).
2) Open the operator-lens panel (compact view): top 3 correlated metrics (qps, kv-warmth, error-rate), one-line hypothesis suggestion (cold cache vs kernel backoff), and a link to the canonical trace anchor for the top percentile.
3) Click trace-anchor -> reveals minimal trace span with contextual tags (route, model-version, seq-len-bucket, tenant-hash). Trace redactors must strip all prompt fields (see privacy note).
4) Run the linked synthetic probe (sandboxed small request) that targets the same model-route/tenant pattern to confirm reproducer.
5) Escalate to rollout policy or run an automated fallback to a compatible quantized model if probe fails.

Metric lexicon (compact; not exhaustive):
- inference.token_latency.quantile.p95: 95th percentile per-token generation latency for route. Tag: model, route, tenant_tier. Unit: ms. Instrumentation: runtime timer aggregated at edge-proxy -> backend.
- inference.kv_cache.hits_ratio: ratio of cache hits for KV cache (per-tenant, per-model). Tag: tenant_id_hash, model. Unit: 0..1. Note: approximate, sampled at eviction events.
- inference.batch.size.avg: average batch size per worker over 1m. Tag: model_variant, hw_pool. Unit: tokens.
- inference.e2e.error_rate: fraction of requests that terminate with non-200 (includes model-fatal, timeout, validation-fail). Tag: error_code, route.
- operator.replay_probe.latency: synthetic reproducer latency. Used to validate hypotheses.

Tracing anchors and design notes:
- Span anchor = a short span with stable semantic tags that are safe to keep long-term. Example tags: {route, model_version, seq_len_bucket, tenant_tier, host_region}. Do NOT include prompt or user content.
- Anchor spans created at edge-proxy -> runtime boundary. We capture span_id and attach a fingerprint for sessionization.
- Sampling: adaptive sampling that prioritizes spans with high token_latency.quantile and low kv_cache.hits_ratio. Default baseline sample rate 0.05 for user traffic; bump to 1.0 for traces that match an active alert rule.
- Privacy: use strict prompt redaction pipeline. Store only a 64-bit hash of canonical prompt shape (e.g., template fingerprint) and length bucket. This is enough to link to a probe definition without storing content.

Dashboard/Widget patterns (operator-lens):
- Compact-lens widget: single-row summary for the alerted route. Shows: current p95, delta vs baseline, kv-warmth, e2e error rate, mini-trace link.
- Drilldown row: time-series for the 3 most predictive metrics (according to correlation window) and a heatmap of seq_len buckets.
- Probe control: button to launch a sandboxed probe and record operator.replay_probe.latency. Probe must run with scrubbed context and with a test key.
- Escape-hatch quick actions: toggle canary fallback, disable model-route, force-evict-kv-cache-for-tier. These are guarded by RBAC and audit log hooks.

Probe definitions (mini-format):
- id: probe-token-warmup-v1
- target: model-route X (region us-west)
content_append:
- payload: generated minimal prompt template (no user PII) with seq_len 32 and deterministic seed
- expected: p95 < baseline + 10% or e2e.error_rate < 0.01

Query budgeting and cost constraints:
- Small operators-only dashboards should default to coarse resolution (1m) and only fetch high-res (10s) for the alerted route on demand.
- Traces should be tiered: hot (full spans for traces matching active incident tags), warm (anchor-only stubs), cold (discard after 7d).

Runbook snippets (for token-latency spikes):
- Step 0: confirm alert source (is it synthetic probe or real traffic?).
- Step 1: check kv_cache.hits_ratio for the tenant tier. If < 0.2 within burst window -> mark hypothesis: cold-cache.
- Step 2: open mini-trace (anchor) and inspect sequence of kernel backoffs and batching. If many small batches -> underbatching from edge.
- Step 3: run replay_probe; if reproduction occurs, try fast mitigation: enable fallback model-variant (policy ID) and notify routing to avoid overloaded pool.
- Step 4: postmortem flags: add synthetic probe for the route to detect recurrence; add metric alert to track probe latency trend.

Implementation TODOs (owner + estimate):
- [Riley] formalize anchor tag schema and implement prompt-redactor (3 wks).
- [Marcus] probe harness that runs in sandboxed infra and reports operator.replay_probe.* (2 wks).
- [Ayesha] dashboard mini-lens prototype in Console (2 wks).
- [Kiran] adaptive tracing sampler integration with alerting layer (2 wks).

Open questions and tradeoffs (notes):
- How precise must tenant hashing be for effective troubleshooting vs. privacy risk? We should prefer consistent hashing across systems but only keep non-reversible hashes.
- Sampling bump strategy: should it be purely rule-driven or also ML-driven (predictive bumping)? Start rule-driven to keep scope small.
- Probe explosion risk: too many probes per route will cost money and noise. Limit to one operator probe per route + automated schedule.

Links/references (internal):
- Confluence: Telemetry Standards (linked above).
- Jira: OBS-412 (anchor schema) and OBS-436 (probe harness).
- Slack thread: #obs-ops (search: "telemetry weave")

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the operator-lens as opinionated UX. Operators want fewer clicks. Provide hypothesis text snippets to speed cognitive load.
- When in doubt, lean to: smaller set of high-signal metrics + safe trace anchors.
- Next sync: obs weekly (2026-01-20) to demo prototype.

Unresolved action items:
- Decide TTL for anchor stubs (7 vs 14 vs 30 days).
- Align RBAC for escape-hatch actions with SRE/Platform security.

End of notebook (for now).

-- Riley
